messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Unusual auth traffic detected for /api/v1/session from multiple regions. Fail rate > 65% over 3m. Paging on-call:

maya (oncall): seeing the alert, pulling up logs now. can someone confirm if this is a routing spike or targeted auth attempts?

sam (sre): tailing auth logs. looks like a large number of `POST /api/v1/session` with failed OAuth token validation. IPs clustered in EU + APAC. not a deploy from our side.

nora (security): please paste a sample log line. we need client_ids, user agents, and whether refresh tokens were attempted.

sam (sre): here are a couple redacted lines:
```
[auth] 2026-09-23T14:12:03Z ip=54.38.12.101 method=POST path=/api/v1/session result=401 client_id=redacted ua="curl/7.68.0"
[auth] 2026-09-23T14:12:04Z ip=3.12.45.200 method=POST path=/api/v1/session result=401 client_id=redacted ua="python-requests/2.25.1"
```

maya (oncall): ok thanks. looks like brute-force token replay rather than credential stuffing (no username enumeration).

carl (eng-runtime): can we throttle by client_id at the edge? I can push a temporary rate-limit if we want to reduce downstream load.

nora (security): yes, do a conservative global rate-limit first (50 req/min per client_id) and reject with 429. we'll want to avoid false positives for customers using wide fanout.

ops-bot: Deploy triggered: `edge-rate-limit v1.2.3` -> canary to 5% in eu-west-1 (initiated by carl).

kevin (support): heads up — we already have two customers on Slack reporting intermittent auth failures. I'll draft a short status update once we confirm mitigation.

maya (oncall): running live look at token validation infra. CPU on auth-validator-1 spiked 4x, queuing visible. suspect replay is causing KV cache thrash.

carl (eng-runtime): adding a short-lived cache warmup and bumping validator instances by +2 in eu-west. doing `kubectl scale` now.

sam (sre): scaled. monitoring metrics. failed auth rate dropping from 65% -> 30% in last 60s. good sign.

nora (security): we should snapshot the offending IPs and IOC list. pulling from logs and will push to firewall block. also request full token validation logs for retrospective.

sec-rotations-bot: Advisory: if any service tokens share the affected IPs' session patterns, schedule rotation. Use `rotations.plan --urgent` to create a rotation ticket.

maya (oncall): quick question — any evidence of successful token reuse (200 responses with different IPs)?

sam (sre): scanning; found ~12 200s where session created then immediately used from a different geo within 30s. marking those as suspicious.

nora (security): assume compromise until proven otherwise. we should rotate potentially exposed refresh tokens for affected customers and prepare a targeted customer outreach list. kevin, work with me on draft.

kevin (support): on it. I'll pull a list of affected orgs by client_id + last successful login. recommend starting with high-privilege customers.

carl (eng-runtime): firewall rule pushed blocking top 200 offending IPs across edge. added temporary `deny` rule in waf for requests matching UA regex `(python-requests|curl|httpie)` with high fail rate. monitor for collateral.

maya (oncall): auth failure rate down to 10%. CPU normalized. good. we still have suspicious 200s flagged. next steps?

nora (security): 1) create a rotation ticket for all service tokens for impacted client_ids. 2) rotate any internal service tokens that might have been seen in logs (we saw one service-to-service token in a debug dump). 3) prepare a legal/comms briefing in case a disclosure is needed.

sec-rotations-bot: Rotation ticket created: ROT-2026-2441 (link: https://internal.rotations/ROT-2026-2441). Owner auto-assigned: carl.

carl (eng-runtime): acknowledged. I'll coordinate token roll, will push new keys to KMS and update services with zero-downtime swap where supported. ETA ~45m.

kevin (support): drafting customer note: short, factual, say we mitigated suspicious activity, rotating tokens for affected customers, no evidence of exfil of customer data so far. will share draft in #customer-notices for review.

maya (oncall): handing off to nora for sec lead. I'll stay on until rotations done.

nora (security): taking lead. timeline: block -> throttle -> scale -> rotation -> customer notice. tagging legal and CS for review. background analysis: collecting full logs and KV cache metrics; will escalate to incident channel if we see any signs of credential harvest or data exfil.

ops-bot: Handoff recorded: oncall transfer maya -> nora at 1888642325.

nora (security): quick ask to infra: please capture a snapshot of auth-validator memory and /proc/pid/fd for the flagged instances, and export oss logs (s3://redwood-incident-logs/1888642000/).

sam (sre): snapshotting now. uploading to s3. link will be available in 10m.

carl (eng-runtime): rotation started. creating feature flag to fallback to read-only tokens for non-critical flows during rotation.

kevin (support): customer notice draft posted to #customer-notices. requesting approvals.

nora (security): we've got a few anomalies in audit logs showing an internal debug key being used from an unexpected IP 52.14.66.77. that's on the rotation list too.

maya (oncall): thanks team. I'll continue monitoring but moving to standby. keep updates here — if anything escalates ping @channel. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in place (throttle + block + scale). severity reduced to P2. follow-up actions: ROT-2026-2441, legal review requested, customer notifications draft.

nora (security): next steps for postmortem: timeline reconstruction, attack vector hypothesis (token replay vs stolen refresh tokens), affected client_id list, retroactive detection rules, and permanent rate-limit rules. assigning postmortem owner in 24h.

kevin (support): will prepare customer-facing summary once legal greenlights wording.

carl (eng-runtime): will complete rotation and signal here when done.

sam (sre): final note — if you see any follow-up alerts with similar fingerprint, escalate to P1. all dashboards bookmarked: https://grafana.internal/d/redwood/auth-traffic

ops-bot: Incident closed for on-call paging at 1888642600 (status: monitoring).

nora (security): closing note: thanks for quick action everyone. we prevented further suspicious successes and have rotation in progress. full postmortem to follow.
